blocks.markdown: **Method.** Analyze whether the claim rests on an **express/implied warranty under the Civil Code**, a **written additional warranty**, a **defect/product-liability provision**, or **more than one legal source**. Each path has different coverage, elements and remedies.

sourceRefs.excerptHint: Civil Code vs. Consumer Act warranties

blocks.markdown: Civil Code Arts. 1546–1547 cover **express warranty and implied warranties of title/hidden defects** — the cross-referenced starting point before reaching the Consumer Act's additional warranties.
The implied warranty of title/eviction sits within the Civil Code cluster cross-referenced by the syllabus; test its elements before, or alongside, any Consumer Act claim.
Civil Code Arts. 1561 onwards address **hidden defects and quality-related remedies**.
Consumer Act Arts. 68–71 govern **additional warranties, including required terms and service warranties**, subject to statutory exceptions.

**Ask** what promise was made, whether it was **in writing**, what **duration and parts/labor scope** were stated, what **standard was breached**, whether **notice/repair was attempted**, and which **remedy the statute authorizes**.

Arts. 97–107 cover **defective products/services and common provisions**. Differentiate **defects in the product itself** from a **failure in the service provided**, then identify the proper remedy and any defenses or common rules.

sourceRefs.excerptHint: Case note: De Guzman v. Toyota Cubao

blocks.markdown: **Civil Code warranty vs. Lemon Law:** general sale warranty rules do **not** replace the Lemon Law's **narrow vehicle coverage and procedure**.
**Warranty term vs. service remedy:** a written warranty's **duration/scope** is different from a statute's separate **process for defective goods/services**.

description: Civil Code warranty cross-references, additional Consumer Act warranties, prohibited acts, and defective products and services.
